_comment: Figma DOES have this — `Head` (23599:392870) on the carts page, pointed out by the user on 2026-08-21. The 2026-08-20 record claimed VERIFIED ABSENT and was wrong: the search ran against the token mirror, which holds colour groups, and a frame that declares no colour group of its own cannot appear there. Absence from the token mirror is not absence from Figma. Rebuilt from the node.

_source.structure: `Head` 390x34, VERTICAL, 16 of side padding. Inside it a 358-wide row holding one HUG column — the title with its own rule directly under it — and then, as the row's sibling, a second rule running the full 358. Two stacked rules, not one line shared between a title and a filler.
_source.gap: 8 between the title and its rule, from `Frame 44470`. The first build used 4, taken from the Frontend's `pb-1`.
_source.accent-color: #E32321 — the rule under the title, 1px on its top edge only.
_source.rule-color: #D4D4D4 = border.accent.gray-light. The first build used border.secondary (#262626), which is near-black — the Frontend's `border-secondary` class, and far too heavy.
_source.title-color: This instance draws the title in #E32321. The Frontend offers primary | secondary and defaults to secondary; the default here follows Figma.

_frontend_evidence.differs_from_figma: The Frontend puts the title and the filler rule side by side on one baseline (`flex items-end`, the title's border-bottom red and the filler's grey). Figma stacks two full rules instead. Figma wins.

_verified_from.scope: the `Head` frame on the carts page, walked to depth 4 with fills, strokes and per-side stroke weights
_verified_from.result: VERIFIED PRESENT. Supersedes the 2026-08-20 record, which said VERIFIED ABSENT after searching only the token mirror. The correction is kept rather than overwritten: the mistake was the method, and the method is what the next check inherits.
